newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr eases vs yen after gaining on mark/yen buying.
newsitem.headline: Dlr eases vs yen after gaining on mark/yen buying.

text.p: 0155 GMT --*Dollar eased against yen by Tokyo mid-morning on profit-taking after drifting higher on mark buying against yen and on expectations of commercial dollar buying at local fixing at 0100 GMT, dealers said.
*Mark also eased against yen after rising above 69.10 yen earlier on buying by Japanese institutional investors.

*Tokyo players see the 200-day moving average at around 116.95 yen as key resistance for dollar/yen, where both Japanese exporters and interbank traders are keen to sell dollars, a trust bank trader said.
*Light, sporadic selling by exporters seen above 116.50 yen but most exporters taking a wait-and-see stance, the trust bank trader said.
*Comments by key Finance Ministry officials seem to suggest Japanese government comfortable with current dollar/yen levels, dealers said.
*Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told news conference that currencies becoming stable as G7 agreement on forex has filtered through to markets.
*Senior MOF official Eisuke Sakakibara also made similar remarks in parliamentary committee meeting today.
0012 GMT --*Dollar drifts up against yen in early Tokyo trade partly due to mark buying against yen and on expectations of commercial dollar buying at 0100 GMT, dealers said.
*No major orders detected so far but one bank dealer said Middle East operators purchased dollar for yen in early trade.
*Fact that dollar briefly rose as high as around 116.72 yen in Toronto amid market holidays in Britain and U.S. also encouraged dollar's rise, said a Japanese bank dealer.
*Profit-taking and light exporter sales likely to emerge at around 116.80 yen, dealers said.
